battle.name: 秦滅
battle.brief: 公元前222年，秦將王翦平定燕國殘部，俘燕王喜，置閩中郡；此前前230滅韓、228滅趙、225滅魏、223滅楚，至前221滅齊，兼并六國的戰爭至此收官。卡面亞述長矛屬前900年前後的新亞述工藝，與本役相隔約一千一百年，並不在戰場上；秦軍所用是弩、長援戈、秦劍、鐵矛與戰車騎兵。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 這場戰爭是秦國對韓、趙、魏、楚、燕、齊六國的滅國戰爭，時間自公元前230年滅韓起，到公元前221年滅齊、秦王政稱皇帝止；卡面所標的公元前222年，是燕國在遼東的殘部被平定、同年在閩越戰役後置閩中郡的一年。秦的一方是關中之國，國君秦王政於公元前246年以十三歲登基，經李斯、尉繚等法家官僚整頓，軍隊由商鞅變法留下的縣制、編戶齊民與軍功爵制支撐：郡縣兵、關中本國兵、六國降兵與徵發的戍卒合流，兵源與糧源都從關中就近調集。六國並非六支各自獨立的隊伍，而是各有專長的常備軍與城防體系：韓國以新鄭為都，弩與機關最為精巧，卻是六國中疆域最小、兵力最弱的一個；趙國都邯鄲，憑李牧與邊軍鐵騎，曾在肥地大破秦軍；魏國都大梁，有以重甲大戟聞名的魏武卒，卻在河西與上郡連失地盤；楚國最後定都壽春，前278年秦將白起拔郢都、燒夷陵後被迫東遷，國力已損大半；燕國都薊，處北方邊地，與匈奴、東胡相接；齊國都臨淄，東海大國，卻長久不修攻戰，士氣鬆弛。戰線之外還有北方匈奴單于頭曼與閩越：前者在秦軍主力南進時不斷掠代地，後者於前222年被秦軍征服而置閩中郡；楚亡之後越國又以船兵助秦攻楚，隨後反為秦所討。秦的敵人並非一支聯軍，而是六套分散的軍政體系，這正是本役戰術安排的基本前提。
countriesEn: This war was the series of campaigns in which the state of Qin destroyed the six states of Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, running from the fall of Han in 230 BC to the surrender of Qi and the enthronement of the first emperor in 221 BC; the year on the card, 222 BC, is the year in which the last remnants of Yan in Liaodong were pacified and in which the commandery of Minzhong was set up after the campaign against the Minyue. On one side stood the state of Qin, seated in Guanzhong and ruled by King Zheng of Qin, who came to the throne at the age of thirteen in 246 BC and who reorganised the whole machinery of government together with Legalist ministers such as Li Si and Wei Jiao; the army rested on the county system, on the registered small peasant households and on the military merit ranks left behind by Shang Yang's reforms, so that county troops, native troops of the Guanzhong heartland, troops surrendered from the conquered states and conscripted levies all merged into a single pool, with both men and grain drawn from close at hand in Guanzhong. The six states were not six independent armies but six separate military and administrative systems, each with its own specialities: Han, capital at Xinzheng, was the most refined in the crossbow and its mechanisms, yet the smallest of the six in territory and the weakest in numbers; Zhao, capital at Handan, could count on Li Mu and its iron-armed frontier cavalry, and had smashed a Qin army at Fei; Wei, capital at Daliang, had the Wei Wuzu, heavy infantry in triple armour carrying great halberds, though it had lost the Hexi and Shangjun corridors to Qin; Chu, which finally made its capital at Shouchun, had already been badly mauled when Bai Qi took Ying and burned Yiling in 278 BC and forced the court eastward; Yan, capital at Ji, sat on the northern frontier in contact with the Xiongnu and the Donghu; Qi, capital at Linzi, was a great eastern state that had long stopped drilling its soldiers and had grown slack in its discipline. Outside the main line stood the Xiongnu under the Chanyu Touman, who raided Dai continually while the Qin army was committed in the south, and the Minyue, conquered in 222 BC and turned into the commandery of Minzhong; after the fall of Chu the state of Yue also lent its marines to help Qin against Chu, only to be turned against in turn. The enemy here was never a single coalition but six dispersed military-political systems, and that is the essential premise on which the tactics of this war were arranged.
people: 決定這場戰爭節奏與次序的是秦王政。他十三歲即位，先在呂不韋、嫪毐與六國反對勢力之間周旋，前238年廢呂不韋，前237年誅嫪毐並收回逐客之令，隨後把李斯、姚賈、頓弱等人招入權力核心，統一戰爭的組織能力由此成形。統兵者是秦國兩代主力：將門王翦與其弟王賦——王翦在壽春外以六十萬大軍築壘待敵，是持久戰的代表；王賦以水攻灌大梁破魏，又自燕南下滅齊，行動最為銳利。副手有蒙武（伐楚、平燕）、李信（前224年率二十萬伐楚，一戰而敗）、掌秦國軍賦的內史騰（主滅韓）與羌瘣，後方徵發與糧秣運轉則由丞相李斯總攝。六國方面的關鍵人物是趙國大將李牧，他以太行山東的邊軍與鐵騎在肥地大破秦軍，卻被趙王遷與其叔父趙嬌的讒言所害，前228年被殺於軍中，趙軍人心隨即崩潰。真正把局面推向不可逆轉的是荊卿刺秦：前227年燕太子丹遣荊卿入咸陽行刺，事敗後秦廷「悉起諸軍」，把北方戰線的兵械全部壓上，燕國在兩年內被掃平。楚國最後的主帥項燕在壽春外大敗，兵敗自殺，楚王負芻被俘；齊王建則在最後關頭選擇不戰而降，齊國因此未經硬仗而亡。背景中還有魏無忌、黃歇、趙武靈王等已故名臣的舊跡，前者曾以魏武卒的組織法度稱雄，趙武靈王的胡服騎射則把騎兵變成六國共有的新軍種。
peopleEn: The man who set the pace and the order of this war was King Zheng of Qin. He came to the throne at thirteen and spent his early years manoeuvring between Lü Buwei, Lao Ai and the opposition in the six states; in 238 BC he deposed Lü Buwei, in 237 BC he executed Lao Ai and revoked the order that had expelled guest foreigners, and then drew men like Li Si, Yao Jia and Dun Ruo into the centre of power. The organisational capacity for a war of unification was formed in that process. The commanders were two generations of the Qin military: the brothers Wang Jian and Wang Ben. Wang Jian, who met and held off Xiang Yan outside Shouchun, brought an army of six hundred thousand men up to a fortified camp and waited behind it, and stood for the doctrine of the protracted battle; Wang Ben broke Daliang against Wei with water and then swept south from Yan to destroy Qi, and was the sharpest of the movers. Their supporting commanders were Meng Wu, who fought in Chu and in Yan, Li Xin, who took two hundred thousand men into Chu in 224 BC and was beaten in a single week, Neishi Teng, who administered the military revenues of Qin and led the attack on Han, and Qiang Zao; the mobilisation of the rear and the movement of grain were in the hands of the chancellor Li Si. The decisive figure on the other side was Li Mu of Zhao, whose frontier troops and iron cavalry broke a Qin army at Fei, but who was destroyed by the slander of King Zhao Qian and his uncle Zhao Jiao and was killed in his camp in 228 BC, whereupon the morale of the Zhao army collapsed. The truly irreversible step was the assassination attempt at Qin: in 227 BC the Crown Prince of Yan sent Jing Ke into Xianyang to strike at the king; when it failed the court 'raised all the armies' and threw the entire military and material weight of the state onto the northern front, and Yan was swept away within two years. Xiang Yan, the last commander of Chu, was beaten outside Shouchun and killed himself, and King Fu Chu of Chu was taken prisoner; King Jian of Qi chose at the last moment not to fight and surrendered, so that Qi perished without a hard-fought battle. In the background stand the traces of worthies already dead, Wei Wuji, Huang Xie and King Wuling of Zhao: the first had made a name through the organisation of the Wei Wuzu, and the second had turned the mounted arm into a new service shared by all six states through his adoption of Scythian dress and cavalry.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛屬新亞述帝國的工藝：短柄、長刃、配鐵鏃，是公元前九世紀前葉的近身刺擊兵器，亞述人把它與弓、盾結合成攻城與野戰的組合。距離本役約一千一百年，它不可能出現在公元前222年的中國戰場；就兵器譜系而言，短柄刺擊器在亞述已是過時形態，而兩河流域的城邑在它之後兩千年內早被更長的直刃兵器取代。真正在場的是秦軍的裝備體系：遠射以弩為首，銅弩機配木臂與矢，弩手前排跪、後排立，與弓兵、持長矛與長援戈的步兵配合成弩陣；近身是秦劍（圓首、菱形格、劍身修長，陝西兵馬俑坑出土數千件）與鐵矛、鐵鍤、斧、鑿；護具以皮甲為主，編綴甲片出自同一批秦墓；重裝備是四馬駕的兵車，車上甲士居中、步兵環衛，秦兵馬俑坑一號坑即存戰車、陶馬與陶俑。攻城手段多樣：撞車、雲梯、穴車（掘地逼近城垣）、弩機射覆城頭，另有灌水一途，用於大梁這類水網城市。載具方面，車兵與騎兵並行，騎兵是趙武靈王胡服騎射之後六國與秦共有的新軍種，馬具齊備；後勤靠牛車、舟船與沿泗水、淮水的水道轉運。六國方面，韓弩最精，趙國有鐵鏃與輕騎，魏武卒依《荀子·議兵》所記「衣三重甲，操十二石之弩，負五石之戈」，楚國殘存大量青銅戈、矛與戟，燕國以弩與游騎守薊，齊國以弓弩與車兵見長。金屬結構上，秦已全面使用鐵器，六國仍多存銅器殘件。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card belongs to the craft of the Neo-Assyrian Empire: a short haft, a long blade and an iron socket, a close-combat thrusting weapon of the early ninth century BC, which the Assyrians combined with the bow and the shield into a set for both siege and field work. At a distance of roughly eleven hundred years from this campaign it could not have been on a Chinese battlefield in 222 BC; in the line of weapon development the short-hafted thrusting arm was already an outmoded form in Assyria, and the cities of the river plains passed to longer straight-edged weapons more than two millennia before the Qin. What was actually present was the equipment system of the Qin army: at the head of the shooting line stood the crossbow, with bronze locks, wooden stocks and bolts, the crossbowmen kneeling in front and standing behind in turn, working with archers and with infantry carrying long spears and long-hafted daggers to form a crossbow line; at close quarters were the Qin swords, round-pommelled with a rhomboid guard and a long blade, of which several thousand have been unearthed from the pits of the terracotta army at Lintong in Shaanxi, together with iron spear-points, picks, axes and chisels; armour was chiefly leather, with the lamellar plates coming from the same tombs; the heavy equipment was the four-horse war chariot with armoured warriors on the platform and infantry around it, and the first pit of the terracotta army preserves chariots, clay horses and figures. Siege methods were varied: battering rams, scaling ladders, tunnel-carts that drove a passage up under the wall, crossbows covering the parapets, and, in one case, the admission of water used against a city like Daliang woven about with waterways. In transport, chariots and cavalry went side by side, the mounted arm being a new kind of service shared by Qin and the other states since King Wuling of Zhao had dressed his troops in Scythian dress, with complete harness; the rear was served by ox-carts, boats and water-borne transport along the Si and the Huai rivers. Among the states, Han was the most refined in its crossbows, Zhao had iron arrowheads and light cavalry, the Wei Wuzu by the account of the Xunzi in the chapter on war wore triple armour, carried a crossbow of twelve stone and a halberd of five stone, Chu still possessed large quantities of bronze daggers, spears and halberds, Yan defended Ji with crossbows and mobile riders, and Qi was known for its bows, crossbows and chariot troops. In metals Qin had gone over to iron throughout, while the other states still carried many bronze pieces.
tactics: 秦軍的部署講究次序：先近後遠、先小後大，先取韓以孤立趙、魏，再圖楚。公元前230年內史騰、羌瘣伐韓，軍隊內外夾擊，新鄭在短時間內陷落，韓王安以國降；韓地素擅弩機的工師隨後被秦廷徵用編入官營，《史記》未記其人數，後世史家多據秦軍弩陣之精而推其來自韓地。對趙用反間：前228年李牧在肥地大破秦軍，秦廷用計使趙王遷懷疑李牧欲反，李牧見殺，趙軍人心崩潰，王翦再攻，邯鄲陷落，趙王遷被俘，降卒遭坑殺。對魏用水攻：前225年王賁率軍東出，圍大梁，引水灌城，魏王假出降，魏國亡；大梁四周為黃河與鴻溝水網，城防倚水為固，秦軍卻用水破之。對楚則先敗後穩：前224年李信以二十萬眾伐楚，輕兵急進、七日而至鄢，楚軍合擊追之，秦軍大敗，士卒死傷過半，李信引兵而還；秦王政於軍旅途中致書王翦謝罪，改以六十萬眾赴淮水，築壘固守不戰，待楚兵氣衰，再整軍出擊，在壽春之外擊潰楚軍，項燕兵敗自殺，楚王負芻被俘，次年楚地盡入於秦。對燕、齊則連成一線：前226年王翦將二十萬眾擊燕，渡易水，燕軍不戰而潰，燕王喜北走保遼東；前222年秦軍追入遼東，平定殘部，燕國亡；前221年王賦自燕南下攻齊，齊不戰而降。兵種配合上，弩陣在前吸住對手，長兵與車兵隨後踏平缺口，騎兵在兩翼包抄與追殺潰兵，渡河用浮橋與舟船，糧道沿泗水、淮水一路接濟，築壘而待是對楚取勝的關鍵。
tacticsEn: The Qin deployment was a matter of order: near before far, small before large, taking Han first in order to isolate Zhao and Wei, and only then turning on Chu. In 230 BC Neishi Teng and Qiang Zao attacked Han, the army pressing in from two sides, Xinzheng fell within a short time and King An of Han surrendered with his state; the crossbow artisans of Han, whose country had been the most skilled in the mechanism, were then called up and entered into Qin's state workshops, though the Shiji records no number for them, and later historians have inferred their origin from the refinement of the Qin crossbow line. Against Zhao the method was the sowing of dissension: in 228 BC Li Mu broke a Qin army at Fei, the Qin court contrived to make King Zhao Qian suspect that Li Mu was plotting rebellion, Li Mu was killed, the morale of the Zhao army collapsed, Wang Jian struck again, Handan fell, King Zhao Qian was taken prisoner and the surrendered men were killed in the pits. Against Wei the Qin used water: in 225 BC Wang Ben led his army east, ringed Daliang and let the water in, King Jia of Wei came out to surrender and Wei perished; the city stood among the waterways of the Yellow River and the Honggou and relied on water for its defence, and Qin broke it with water. Against Chu there was first defeat and then steadiness: in 224 BC Li Xin took two hundred thousand men into Chu, racing ahead with a light force and reaching Yu in seven days; the Chu concentrated and pursued, the Qin army was beaten, more than half its men were killed or wounded, and Li Xin withdrew; the king of Qin wrote to Wang Jian to apologise in person, then sent him with six hundred thousand to the Huai, where he built a camp, held fast and did not fight, waited for the Chu army to tire, and then marched out to smash it outside Shouchun, where Xiang Yan was beaten and killed himself and King Fu Chu of Chu was taken prisoner; the following year the lands of Chu passed wholly into Qin. Against Yan and Qi the armies were run on a single line: in 226 BC Wang Jian took two hundred thousand men against Yan, crossed the Yi River, the Yan troops broke without a battle and King Xi fled north to hold Liaodong; in 222 BC the Qin pursued into Liaodong, pacified the last remnants and Yan perished; in 221 BC Wang Ben moved south from Yan against Qi, and Qi surrendered without a battle. In the combination of arms the crossbow line absorbed the enemy's attention in front, the long weapons and the chariots followed into the breach, cavalry on the two flanks turned the pursuit and caught the routed, rivers were crossed on pontoon bridges and boats, the line of supply ran along the Si and the Huai, and the holding of a fortified camp while waiting was the key to victory over Chu.
data: 可以依據的數字大致如下。整場兼并戰爭自公元前230年滅韓起，到公元前221年滅齊止，歷九年；本卡所標的公元前222年，是燕國在遼東的殘部被平定、閩中被置為郡的年份，秦軍在該年並進兩役，一在東北遼東，一在東南閩越。秦軍最高的一次兵力記載是王翦伐楚的六十萬眾，見於《史記·秦始皇本紀》；此前李信伐楚為二十萬眾，據《史記·白起王翦列傳》，其軍兼程急進、七日而至鄢，隨即被楚軍追敗，士卒死傷過半。破趙之役，趙國降卒遭坑殺，人數各書不一，記為十餘萬至四十餘萬，本卡不取其精確數。後世文獻以「秦兵不過百萬，卒不過五十萬」概括秦國兵員規模（《淮南子》一系有近似說法，出處與斷句各家不一），那是全國常備與徵發的總量，絕非一時投入一役之數。戰國末年人口，學界一般估在數千萬量級，約兩千萬至三千萬，說法不一。由咸陽出兵的距離，按古里約合今半公里計：至壽春約一千九百里，至薊約二千二百里，至臨淄約一千六百里，實際行程遠比直線為長。關中糧食供應倚靠鄭國渠與都江堰兩項水利，《史記·河渠書》稱鄭國渠成「溉田四萬餘頃」，都江堰則約前256年李冰任蜀守時興工；南征的糧食靠鴻溝、泗水、淮水轉運。年月方面，《史記》本紀只記年不記月，卡面所標月份屬後世編年推算，本卡取通行的一說。總傷亡數字無可靠記載，六國各軍覆滅多以十萬人計。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The war of conquest as a whole runs from the fall of Han in 230 BC to the fall of Qi in 221 BC, nine years; the year on the card, 222 BC, is the year in which the Yan remnants in Liaodong were pacified and Minzhong was made into a commandery, the Qin army carrying out two campaigns in that year, one in the north-east at Liaodong and one in the south-east against the Minyue. The largest Qin force on record is the six hundred thousand men with which Wang Jian campaigned against Chu, given in the annals of the First Qin Emperor; the earlier expedition of Li Xin into Chu was two hundred thousand, and by the account in the Shiji biography of Bai Qi and Wang Jian his army advanced at forced pace and reached Yu in seven days, was then pursued and beaten by the Chu, and lost more than half its men in killed and wounded. In the fall of Zhao the surrendered men were killed in the pits, the number given differently from book to book, from a hundred thousand odd to four hundred thousand odd, and no precise figure is taken here. Later literature summarises the size of Qin's military in the phrase 'no more than a million in arms and no more than five hundred thousand foot' (a similar statement appears in works of the Huainanzi school, though its source and its exact wording are disputed), and that is the total of the standing and conscripted forces of the whole state and never the number committed to a single operation. The population of the late Warring States period is generally put by scholars in the range of several tens of millions, roughly twenty to thirty million, with much disagreement. The distances marched out of Xianyang, the old li being about half a modern kilometre, are some nineteen hundred li to Shouchun, some twenty-two hundred li to Ji and some sixteen hundred li to Linzi, and the actual route was very much longer than the straight line. The grain of the Qin army came from two hydraulic works in Guanzhong: the Zhengguo Canal, which the Shiji on the rivers records as irrigating more than forty thousand qing when completed, and the Dujiangyan works, begun about 256 BC when Li Bing held the office of governor of Shu; for the southern campaigns the grain was moved along the Honggou, the Si and the Huai. As for the months of the fighting, the main annals of the Shiji record the year and not the month; the month given on the card belongs to a later chronological reckoning, and the current common reading has been taken. There is no reliable figure for the total losses; the armies of the six states were destroyed, and their losses are counted by the tens of thousands.
cause: 秦之所以能以一國之力吃掉六國，是數百年變革累積的結果。制度上，商鞅變法把軍功與爵祿、田宅掛鈎，把編戶齊民的小家庭與獎勵耕織的政策組織成能持續產兵的國家機器；關中良田所出粟米，支撐起一支又一支遠征大軍。地理上，關中四塞，出函谷、崤山、天水、隴山可守，進可沿河、汾、沂東出中原，退可倚巴蜀與關中平原；約前256年李冰修都江堰、前246年開鑿鄭國渠，關中遂成大糧倉，遠征才有底氣。戰略上，范雎「遠交近攻」、張儀連橫離間六國、白起多年攻魏拔河西、攻楚拔郢，逐一削去了六國的屏障。國際上，六國雖有合縱之約，卻各懷算計，合縱一散，秦即各個擊破。內部則是六國君主的失能：趙王遷親讒殺李牧，楚王負芻糊塗，齊王建晏安不修攻戰，韓王安無兵可用。公元前237年的逐客令與李斯《諫逐客書》所促成的反轉，則顯示秦廷不但有打遍六國的物力，也有吸納天下人才的制度自信。
causeEn: The fact that a single state could swallow six lay in centuries of accumulated change. In institutions, Shang Yang's reforms tied military merit to rank, land and houses, and organised the small peasant households and the policy of rewarding agriculture and war into a state machine capable of producing troops continuously; the grain of the good fields of Guanzhong sustained great armies on campaign after campaign. In geography, Guanzhong was girded by passes, defensible at Hangu, Xiaoshan, Tianshui and Longshan, able to strike out into the central plain along the Yellow River, the Fen and the Yi, and to fall back on Ba-Shu and the Guanzhong plain; after Li Bing worked the Dujiangyan about 256 BC and the Zhengguo Canal was cut in 246 BC, Guanzhong became a great granary, and only then were distant campaigns possible at all. In strategy, Fan Ju's policy of befriending the distant and attacking the near, Zhang Yi's crossings and separations among the six states, and Bai Qi's years of taking the Hexi from Wei and the Ying from Chu had already shaved away the shields of the others. Internationally, though the six states formed coalitions, each kept its own counsel, and when the coalitions dissolved Qin simply took them one at a time. Internally too the rulers of the six had failed: King Zhao Qian listened to slander and killed Li Mu, King Fu Chu of Chu was muddled, King Jian of Qi sat idly and did not drill, and King An of Han had no troops to speak of. The expulsion of guest foreigners ordered in 237 BC and the reversal of that order after the memorial of Li Si show that the Qin court had not only the material to defeat the six but also the institutional confidence to draw talent from everywhere.
impact: 兼并的直接後果，是中國第一次出現一個橫跨原六國的單一帝國，疆域東至海、西抵臨洮、北到河套、南至南海。秦隨即在廢分封、設郡縣的基礎上推行同一套制度：小篆統一文字、車同軌、度量衡與錢幣標準化；這套制度經漢承秦制一路傳到隋唐，成為後世王朝行政的骨架。國防上，蒙恬於前215年前後將三十萬眾北擊匈奴、取河南地，「卻匈奴七百餘里」（里程為古記，換算難確），隨後築長城連接秦、趙、燕舊塞；南方則略取陸梁、置桂林象郡南海郡，把華北的農耕、中原的商市與岭南連成一體。代價也立刻顯現：同一套以軍功與徭役驅動的體制，在統一之後從對外作戰轉為對內徵發，長城、靈渠、陵墓與軍役同時開工，全國負擔驟然加重。思想控制隨之而來，前213年有焚書之議，前212年有坑儒之舉；而新占地區的六國遺民與關中民眾的怨望同時累積，前209年大澤鄉起義爆發，前207年秦亡。歷史的吊詭正在於：秦滅六國靠的是同時代最有效的組織能力，而秦的速亡也源於同一份能力。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the conquest was the first appearance in China of a single empire spanning the lands of all six former states, reaching from the eastern sea to Lintao in the west, north to the Hetao and south to the South Sea. Qin then built on the abolition of the feudal grants and the setting up of commanderies to enforce one system throughout: a uniform script in small seal form, the same gauge of wheels, and standardised measures, weights and coinage; this system, which the Han inherited from the Qin and carried on to the Sui and the Tang, became the skeleton of the administration of every later Chinese dynasty. In defence, Meng Tian drove the Xiongnu back in about 215 BC, leading three hundred thousand men north against them, taking the land south of the Hetao and 'holding them back more than seven hundred li' (a figure from the ancient records, hard to convert), and then built the Great Wall to join the old walls of Qin, Zhao and Yan; in the south the realm took the land of Luliang and set up the commanderies of Guilin, Xiang and Nanhai, knitting the farming of northern China, the markets of the central plain and Lingnan into one. The cost appeared at once as well: the same apparatus that had been driven by military merit and corvée labour in the wars now turned inward, and the Great Wall, the Lingqu canal, the mausoleums and the military levies were all started at once, with the burden on the whole country rising sharply. Ideological control followed, with the proposal to burn books in 213 BC and the burying of scholars in 212 BC; and the resentment of the peoples of the conquered states and of the Guanzhong commoners accumulated together, until the Dazexiang rising broke out in 209 BC and the Qin fell in 207 BC. The irony of history lies in this: the conquest of the six states was won by the most effective organisation the age could produce, and the swift fall of the Qin was produced by that same organisation.
result: 結果是一場乾淨利落的連鎖崩解。前230年韓亡，韓王安被俘；前228年趙亡，李牧死、邯鄲陷落、趙王遷被俘；前225年魏亡，大梁被水灌破，魏王假出降；前223年楚亡，項燕兵敗自殺，楚王負芻被俘；前222年燕亡，薊城與遼東盡入秦軍，燕王喜被俘後廢為庶人，流放而死；同年閩越戰役後置閩中郡；前221年齊不戰而降，齊王建被遷於松柏之間，兼并戰爭以秦王政稱皇帝、置郡縣告終。戰法上的總結很清楚：以分階段的次序避免兩面作戰，以反間除去對方的支柱，以築壘待敵消耗楚軍，以水攻破大梁，以騎兵與車兵追擊潰兵，最後以編戶齊民與郡縣把新得的土地與人口固定下來。長期看，這一役是中國由諸侯並立走向帝國的轉折點：秦的行政框架在兩代之內崩解，漢承其制，帝國時代由此真正開始。
resultEn: The result was a clean chain of collapse. Han perished in 230 BC and King An of Han was taken prisoner; Zhao perished in 228 BC, Li Mu was killed, Handan fell and King Zhao Qian was taken prisoner; Wei perished in 225 BC, Daliang was broken by the water and King Jia of Wei came out to surrender; Chu perished in 223 BC, Xiang Yan was beaten and killed himself and King Fu Chu was taken prisoner; Yan perished in 222 BC, Ji and Liaodong passed to the Qin army, King Xi of Yan was taken prisoner, stripped of his rank and died in exile; in the same year the Minyue were defeated and Minzhong made into a commandery; Qi surrendered without a battle in 221 BC, King Jian of Qi was moved to the place called Songbai, and the war of conquest ended with the king of Qin taking the title of emperor and setting up commanderies. The lesson of the method is clear: to fight in stages so as never to be opposed on two fronts, to destroy the enemy's pillar by sowing dissension, to wear out the Chu army by holding behind a wall, to break Daliang with water, to chase the routed with cavalry and chariots, and finally to fix the newly taken lands and people by the registration of households and by commanderies. In the long run the campaign was the turning point at which China passed from a world of competing lords to an empire: the administrative frame of the Qin broke down within two generations, the Han took up its system, and the imperial age properly began.
